module.title: Bacterial methionine cycle and homocysteine remethylation
module.description: A reusable bacterial cycle that converts L-methionine to S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM), channels SAM through methyl-transfer reactions that produce S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH), hydrolyzes SAH to L-homocysteine, and remethylates L-homocysteine to regenerate L-methionine. The boundary begins with methionine adenosylation and ends with methionine regeneration; de novo production of methionine and sulfur assimilation are adjacent pathways rather than parts of this cycle.

evidence.title: ECOLI luxS gene review
evidence.statement: The completed E. coli luxS review grounds LuxS as the cytosolic S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase that releases L-homocysteine for methionine regeneration.

connections.description: SAM produced by MetK is the methyl donor used in transmethylation.
Transmethylation produces SAH for either bacterial processing route.
Complete SAH processing supplies homocysteine for remethylation.
Remethylation regenerates methionine for another cycle.

module.notes: This bacterial module is intentionally separate from the existing eukaryotic methionine_cycle, sam_cycle, and homocysteine_metabolism modules. De novo methionine biosynthesis remains in methionine_biosynthesis. Cysteine biosynthesis, transsulfuration, sulfur assimilation, methionine degradation, and methylthioadenosine salvage are outside this cycle boundary.

knowledge_gaps.gap_statement: The distribution and physiological use of direct AhcY versus the two-step MtnN/Pfs-LuxS route vary across bacterial lineages and growth conditions.
knowledge_gaps.boundary: A genome satisfies the two-step route only when both MtnN/Pfs and LuxS are supported; isolated MtnN-family proteins also used in MTA salvage do not establish a complete methionine-cycle route.

document.description: metE (PP_2698) encodes a compact single-barrel MetE-like enzyme predicted to catalyze cobalamin-independent methylation of L-homocysteine to L-methionine. It contains the conserved C-terminal/archaeal-type MetE catalytic barrel and zinc site rather than the canonical bacterial two-barrel architecture, so its activity is currently supported by domain, residue, and pathway evidence rather than direct KT2440 biochemical characterization.

review.summary: Cobalamin-independent methionine synthase activity is the best predicted function for this compact MetE-like catalytic barrel.
review.reason: PP_2698 is a 344-aa protein whose single Pfam PF01717/Meth_synt_2 domain (residues 5-329) is the cobalamin-independent methionine synthase C-terminal/archaeal-type catalytic barrel; it also matches InterPro IPR016456 (Met_Synthase_cat), PIRSF005632 and the CDD CIMS C-terminal-like model. The argument for the activity is this family membership (the catalytic barrel carries the zinc/homocysteine site in characterized MetE enzymes); activity has not been directly tested in KT2440, and PIRSF labels the family as predicted. The submitted product name (ECO:0000313) is not cited.

suggested_questions.question: What is the physiological fate of the 5-methylthioribose produced by Pfs in E. coli K-12? Should the Pfs SAH-to-S-ribosylhomocysteine reaction carry any AI-2 or quorum-sensing process annotation, or should quorum sensing remain restricted to LuxS-catalyzed DPD production and AI-2 response?

Should GO add a substrate-specific child of EC 3.2.2.9 for 5'-deoxyadenosine nucleosidase activity, analogous to the existing S-adenosylhomocysteine and methylthioadenosine nucleosidase terms, so Pfs-mediated repair of radical SAM byproduct accumulation can be curated as a molecular function?

document.description: LuxS is the cytosolic S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase of the bacterial activated methyl cycle. It cleaves S-ribosylhomocysteine to L-homocysteine and 4,5-dihydroxy-2,3-pentadione, regenerating homocysteine for methionine recycling and producing the precursor that spontaneously cyclizes to the AI-2 quorum-sensing signal.

review.summary: The family-level InterPro inference that LuxS binds iron is consistent with the conserved LuxS metalloenzyme fold.
review.reason: LuxS-family S-ribosylhomocysteine lyases use a divalent metal center, and UniProt records this E. coli enzyme as binding one Fe cation per subunit. The cofactor binding is real but supports the catalytic lyase activity rather than constituting a separate core molecular function.

review.summary: The DnaK interaction comes from a large-scale affinity-purification/mass spectrometry network and does not identify a specific LuxS activity.
review.reason: The reported physical interaction is not evidence for a narrower molecular function than the low-information parent term protein binding, and LuxS is a metabolic lyase rather than a DnaK co-chaperone or dedicated adaptor.

review.summary: The PAINT cytosol assertion fits the soluble, cytosolic activated methyl cycle chemistry performed by LuxS.
review.reason: LuxS has its own curated cytosol evidence in E. coli and belongs to a bacterial S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase clade whose activity is inherited from the same cytosolic state; the target's presence in the IBA WITH/FROM is expected because target-specific evidence helped seed the PAINT node.

review.summary: Automated UniProt rules correctly associate LuxS-family enzymes with AI-2 quorum-sensing signal biosynthesis.
review.reason: LuxS participates in quorum sensing by generating 4,5-dihydroxy-2,3-pentadione, the precursor that yields AI-2 signal molecules; this process role is a direct consequence of its S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase activity.

review.summary: An E. coli luxS mutant unable to synthesize AI-2 was used to define AI-2-responsive transcription.
review.reason: Loss of luxS blocks synthesis of the AI-2 signal and thereby places LuxS upstream of the quorum-sensing response. LuxS performs the AI-2 producer step rather than signal detection, but production of the extracellular signal is part of the quorum-sensing process.

supported_by.supporting_text: We investigated global changes in mRNA abundance elicited by the AI-2 signaling molecule through the use of a luxS mutant that was unable to synthesize AI-2.

review.summary: The PAINT inference captures the family-defining LuxS activity at the correct level of specificity.
review.reason: E. coli LuxS is experimentally supported as an S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase, and there is no evidence of target-specific loss or divergence that would challenge the PAINT node placement.

review.summary: Schauder et al. directly established the LuxS substrate and products in the AI-2 biosynthetic pathway.
review.reason: The paper identifies LuxS as the enzyme that cleaves S-ribosylhomocysteine to homocysteine plus the AI-2 precursor/product, exactly matching GO:0043768.

supported_by.supporting_text: The substrate for LuxS is S-ribosylhomocysteine, which is cleaved to form two products, one of which is homocysteine, and the other is AI-2.

review.summary: RHEA, EC, InterPro, and UniRule all point to the experimentally verified LuxS S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase activity.
review.reason: The automated assertion is specific and is corroborated by the experimental E. coli annotation and the PAINT family assertion for the same activity.

review.summary: The E. coli and Vibrio harveyi luxS genes encode homologous AI-2 production proteins.
review.reason: The sequence-similarity assertion is consistent with the original cross-species identification of luxS as an AI-2 production gene family and with the later direct E. coli biochemical annotation.

supported_by.supporting_text: Here we report the identification and analysis of the gene responsible for AI-2 production in V. harveyi, S. typhimurium, and E. coli.

review.summary: This broad InterPro metal-binding call is directionally correct but less specific than the existing iron ion binding annotation.
review.reason: LuxS is a metal-dependent S-ribosylhomocysteine lyase with one inferred Fe cation per subunit, so GO:0005506 captures the cofactor more precisely than generic metal ion binding.

review.summary: LuxS directly releases homocysteine from S-ribosylhomocysteine in the bacterial two-step SAH-processing route of the activated methyl cycle.
review.reason: LuxS catalyzes the second MtnN/Pfs-LuxS route step, producing L-homocysteine that can be remethylated to regenerate L-methionine after SAM-dependent methyl transfer.
